extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers (referees) for Nature Portfolio journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for peer reviewers assessing manuscripts submitted to Nature Portfolio journals, including what to report, confidentiality/anonymity rules, editorial process expectations, and policies on AI, timing, and review formats (double-anonymized/transparent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper should represent an advance in understanding likely to influence thinking in the field, with strong evidence for its conclusions; there should be a discernible reason why the work deserves the visibility of publication in a Nature Portfolio journal rather than the best of the specialist journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers must show conceptual advance and strong supporting evidence; consider both novelty/importance and why Nature Portfolio-level visibility is merited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial desk rejection grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may reject promptly without external review papers judged to be of insufficient general interest or otherwise inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desk rejection may be based on informal advice from specialists; common reasons include specialist interest, lack of novelty, insufficient conceptual advance, or major technical/interpretational problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of reviewers in editorial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the editors with the information needed to reach a decision; set out arguments for and against publication rather than only a direct recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most useful reports explain reasoning and weigh pros and cons; editors evaluate strength of arguments rather than counting votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to follow-up reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers agree to assess a paper they are considered committed to review subsequent revisions and to provide follow-up advice if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be willing to respond to further requests; editors may not return resubmissions to reviewers if authors have not made a serious attempt to address criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting peer-reviewers — selection factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors select reviewers based on expertise, reputation, specific recommendations and their own experience of a reviewer's characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred referees are quick, careful, and provide reasoning for their views (whether critical or forgiving); Springer Nature is committed to diverse demographic representation when choosing reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to literature for review
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer lacks access to a published paper necessary for evaluation, the journal will obtain and supply a copy upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should send the publication reference to the handling editor who will obtain the paper (paying any necessary fees) and forward it to the reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key results — reporting outstanding features
rubrics_metrics.description: Please summarise what you consider to be the outstanding features of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a succinct statement of the manuscript's main contributions and most important results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity — identify fatal flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the manuscript have flaws which should prohibit its publication? If so, provide details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify any technical, methodological, or interpretational flaws that undermine the paper's validity and justify why they preclude publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the conclusions are not original, provide relevant references. Subjectively, assess whether the results are of immediate interest to many in the discipline and/or to several disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on novelty, place in literature, and breadth of interest; supply references when noting lack of originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data & methodology — transparency and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the validity of the approach, quality of the data and quality of presentation; reviewers are expected to review all data, including extended data and supplementary information. Is reporting sufficiently detailed and transparent to enable reproducing the results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether experimental/methodological descriptions and data availability enable replication; flag missing details or problematic presentation of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of statistics and treatment of uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: All error bars should be defined in corresponding figure legends; reviewers should comment on appropriateness of statistical tests and accuracy of description of error bars and probability values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific comments about statistical methodology, whether tests are appropriate, whether uncertainties are correctly presented and interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions — robustness and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the conclusions and data interpretation are robust, valid and reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate if conclusions are supported by the data and analyses, and whether alternative interpretations have been considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: List additional experiments or data that could help strengthen the work in a revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete, prioritized recommendations for experiments, analyses, or clarifications that would address weaknesses or increase impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: References — completeness and appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this manuscript reference previous literature appropriately? If not, what references should be included or excluded?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify missing key citations, incorrect attributions, or unnecessary references; provide specific literature to add or remove where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and context — abstract/introduction/conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the abstract clear and accessible? Are the abstract, introduction and conclusions appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on readability, structure, and whether the paper places results in proper context for its intended readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflammatory or potentially libelous material
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the manuscript contain any language that is inappropriate or potentially libelous?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag wording that could be defamatory or unduly inflammatory and recommend rephrasing or removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity and inclusion concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise any concerns that may have an impact on Springer Nature's commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion (for example, geographic/gender/ethnic representation implications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note omissions or biases that affect DEI and suggest corrective changes where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/expertise disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate any particular part of the manuscript, data, or analyses that you feel is outside the scope of your expertise, or that you were unable to assess fully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about limitations of your assessment so editors can seek additional expert advice if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to editor's specific questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please address any other specific question asked by the editor via email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor parts of the report to bespoke editorial requests (e.g., selectivity, suitability, specific technical points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential comments to the editor are welcome, but they should not contradict the main points as stated in the comments for transmission to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the confidential section for sensitive advice or candid appraisal for editors, but keep author-facing comments consistent with confidential remarks' substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and justification of statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should document the referees’ thought process; all statements should be justified and argued in detail, naming facts and citing supporting references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give evidence and reasoning for claims in the report; provide citations where asserting prior art or methodological critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use by peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should not upload manuscripts into generative AI tools; if any part of the evaluation was supported by an AI tool, reviewers must declare the use transparently in the peer review report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors emphasize reviewers' accountability for accuracy and limits of generative AI; contact editor if unsure about appropriate AI usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to respond promptly within the number of days agreed and to inform the editor if they anticipate a longer delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely responses help editors manage the process; notify editors early to allow finding alternatives if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and revealing identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees' identities are not released to authors or other reviewers unless a referee voluntarily signs their comments; reviewers should not identify themselves to authors while the manuscript is under consideration without the editor's knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before signing, consider that reports (signed or not) are shared with other reviewers and across journals on transfer; revealing identity may complicate future interactions and discussions of revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the peer-review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors, authors and reviewers are required to keep confidential all details of the editorial and peer review process on submitted manuscripts; correspondence, referees' reports and other confidential material must not be published or disclosed without prior written consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking advice from colleagues, consult the editor first and provide the names of any such colleagues with the final report; note legal limits to guaranteed confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-anonymized peer review option
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Nature-branded and Communications journals offer double-anonymized peer review; authors who choose this option remain anonymous to referees and are responsible for anonymizing their manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A checklist is provided to authors to help anonymize manuscripts; reviewers should follow journal-specific instructions when assessing double-anonymized submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review option
rubrics_metrics.description: Several Nature journals offer transparent peer review, publishing details about the peer review process (reviewer comments, author rebuttals, and sometimes editorial decision letters); authors may opt in at completion of peer review before acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all journals apply this uniformly; peer review files published will not contain confidential editorial discussions or confidential comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing referees' reports policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio does not suppress reviewers' reports; on rare occasions reports may be edited to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information about other matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are asked to avoid statements that may cause needless offence but are strongly encouraged to state their opinion plainly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reviewers and transfer of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions selected for peer review are sent to at least one, but usually two or more, independent reviewers; when manuscripts are transferred between Nature Portfolio journals, referee comments are transferred and, for transfers between in-house editors, referee identities may also be transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can suggest reviewers and request exclusions; the editor's choice is final; reviewers should be aware that comments may accompany manuscript transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics, security and seeking additional advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may seek advice on aspects that raise ethical concerns, data or materials access issues, or societal/security implications; such advice is sought concurrently with technical review and the editor makes the ultimate decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should flag ethical or security concerns; editors may request specialist advice beyond technical reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-level goals of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is designed to select technically valid research of significant interest; referees are expected to identify flaws, suggest improvements and assess novelty to ensure internal consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance stringency and openness to novel ideas; recognize limitations of peer review (cannot reliably detect cleverly concealed fraud) and focus on improving scientific quality and clarity.
